title: A minor-monotone parameter characterizing integral Erdős–Pósa duality
formal: Historical conjecture, resolved positively: for every fixed nonempty finite graph H, does there exist a minor-monotone graph parameter p_H taking nonnegative integer values such that, for every minor-closed graph class C, H-minor models have the integral Erdős–Pósa property on C if and only if sup_{G∈C}p_H(G)<∞? The same parameter p_H must work for all choices of C.
context:
Packing asks for many vertex-disjoint occurrences of H as a minor. Covering asks for a small common vertex set meeting every such occurrence. An Erdős–Pósa function says that bounded packing forces bounded covering throughout a whole graph class.

Choosing a separate arbitrary parameter after seeing C would weaken the conjecture. Here H alone determines p_H, and boundedness of that one parameter recognizes every minor-closed class where the duality holds.

Paul, Protopapas, Thilikos and Wiederrecht give a finite collection of obstruction sequences for every proper minor-closed target class. A minor-closed environment has integral packing–covering duality precisely when it excludes some member of every sequence. Applying this to H-minor-free target graphs yields the conjectured parameter.

Half-integral packing allows each vertex to belong to two chosen models. The source paper’s half-integral results alone do not settle this card. The later theorem characterizes the integral duality required here. For planar H, the classical integral theorem already holds on all graphs, so the constant parameter p_H=0 suffices.
why: Provides a uniform structural explanation for which minor-closed graph classes support integral packing–covering duality for a fixed graph pattern.
status_note: Resolved as a consequence of Paul–Protopapas–Thilikos–Wiederrecht, Obstructions to Erdős–Pósa Dualities for Minors, FOCS 2024, Theorem 1.1 in the full version. Checked the original conjecture, integral EP-pair definition, finite obstruction-sequence characterization and its application to H-minor-free graphs, including disconnected H. This is a published-theorem/model match, not an independent proof audit or proof-assistant certificate.

progress.text: The ICALP paper states the minor-monotone parameter characterization as Conjecture 1.
The full obstruction-sequence theorem in arXiv:2407.09671v2 yields the required parameter when the target class consists of H-minor-free graphs.
The result is published at FOCS 2024, pp. 31–52.

sentences: An Erdős–Pósa property turns a bound on disjoint graph-pattern occurrences into a bound on the vertices needed to hit every occurrence.
The conjecture asked for one minor-monotone parameter for each pattern H that recognizes exactly the minor-closed classes with this property.
The parameter must work uniformly across all such classes.
The same authors’ later FOCS 2024 obstruction theorem gives the required characterization.
This settles the integral question, beyond the earlier half-integral result.

references.title: Delineating Half-Integrality of the Erdős-Pósa Property for Minors: The Case of Surfaces
references.authors: Paul, Christophe; Protopapas, Evangelos; Thilikos, Dimitrios M.; Wiederrecht, Sebastian

definitions: Graphs are finite, undirected and simple. A minor is obtained by deleting vertices or edges and contracting edges, with loops removed and parallel edges suppressed. An H-minor model in G consists of pairwise disjoint connected vertex sets B_v for v∈V(H), with an edge between B_u and B_v for each uv∈E(H); its support is their union. Let pack_H(G) be the largest number of models with mutually disjoint supports, and let τ_H(G) be the minimum number of vertices whose deletion leaves no H minor. The integral Erdős–Pósa property on C means that a function f:N_0→N_0 exists such that τ_H(G)≤f(pack_H(G)) for every G∈C. This one f may depend on H and C, but not on the individual graph. A class is minor-closed if it contains every minor of each of its graphs. A graph parameter is invariant under graph isomorphism and is minor-monotone when G′ a minor of G implies p_H(G′)≤p_H(G). Boundedness on C means one finite bound for all graphs in C. H need not be connected. No efficient evaluation algorithm or uniquely prescribed parameter is part of the conjecture.
answer_criterion: The affirmative answer follows from the published finite obstruction-sequence characterization: for the target class of H-minor-free graphs, take p_H(G) to be the largest order of an obstruction in its fixed finite collection of increasing minor sequences that occurs as a minor of G, using 0 when none occurs. Minor monotonicity and the theorem’s excluded-sequence criterion give exactly the required equivalence.
